preconditions.description: n is the length of the string (1 ≤ n ≤ 100,000) and k is the maximum number of allowed character changes (0 ≤ k ≤ n).

preconditions.expression: all(c in {'a', 'b'} for c in s)
preconditions.description: The string s consists only of characters 'a' and 'b'.

postconditions.description: The output is the maximum beauty achievable by changing at most k characters in the string, where beauty is defined as the maximum length of a substring of equal characters ('a' or 'b').

postconditions.expression: max_beauty == max(len(substring) for substring in possible_substrings(s, k))
postconditions.description: The maximum beauty is the length of the longest possible substring of equal characters ('a' or 'b') that can be formed by changing at most k characters in the original string.
